name: Ego Leader - Strict Synchrony
description: Decision authority: unilateral leadership by ego. Landmark choice: ego selects i* = argmin_i ( distance(ego_agent_position, landmark_positions[i]) + distance(other_agent_position, landmark_positions[i]) ). This picks a landmark that minimizes total travel for both agents. Execution: ego_agent_position moves toward landmark_positions[i*] along the straight line at its current speed. other_agent_position observes ego's heading and mirrors by targeting the same landmark i*, using a proportional control toward landmark_positions[i*]. Synchrony rule: enforce strict simultaneous arrival by aligning predicted arrival times. Compute t_E = dist(ego_agent_position, landmark_positions[i*]) / |ego_agent_velocity| and t_O = dist(other_agent_position, landmark_positions[i*]) / |other_agent_velocity|. Adjust speeds so that t_O ≈ t_E within a small tolerance (e.g., 0.01 s). If Blue would arrive earlier, it slows down and waits near the landmark; if it would arrive later, it speeds up to meet Ego’s arrival. No explicit messages are exchanged; coordination emerges from leader selection and implicit timing.

name: Ego Leader - Tolerant Synchrony
description: Decision authority: unilateral leadership by ego. Landmark choice: same as in the strict version (i* = argmin_i dist(ego, Li) + dist(other, Li)). Execution: ego moves toward landmark_positions[i*] as the leader. Synchrony rule: tolerant arrival with a waiting buffer τ (e.g., 0.5 s). Each step, estimate t_E and t_O as in the strict case. If |t_O − t_E| ≤ τ, proceed and arrive within the tolerance window. If t_O < t_E − τ, Blue slows to delay arrival; if t_O > t_E + τ, Blue speeds up. If Blue would arrive too early, it waits near the landmark within a small radius until Ego arrives, then both proceed to the landmark (or complete arrival). No explicit communication is used.

name: Equally Shared Decision - Strict Synchrony
description: Decision authority: egalitarian (shared influence). Landmark choice: for each landmark i, compute d_i = ( dist(ego_agent_position, Li) + dist(other_agent_position, Li) ) / 2 and pick i* = argmin_i d_i. Both agents influence the choice equally by averaging their distances to each landmark. Execution: both ego and other move toward landmark_positions[i*]. Synchrony rule: enforce strict simultaneity by setting a common target arrival time t* = max( dist(ego_agent_position, landmark_positions[i*]), dist(other_agent_position, landmark_positions[i*]) ) / v_ref, where v_ref is a reasonable cruising speed (or their current speeds averaged). Each agent adjusts its speed so that its own travel time equals t*. If one is closer, it reduces speed to match the other’s arrival time. No explicit communication; coordination arises from equal weighting and a shared target.

name: Equally Shared Decision - Tolerant Synchrony
description: Decision authority: egalitarian (shared influence). Landmark choice: same averaging criterion as the strict egalitarian strategy to pick i* = argmin_i ( dist(Ego, Li) + dist(Other, Li) ) / 2. Execution: both agents head toward landmark_positions[i*]. Synchrony rule: tolerant arrival with a small window. Compute t_E and t_O as before. Allow a delay window δ (e.g., 0.5 s) for arrival. If the predicted arrival times differ by more than δ, adjust speeds to reduce the difference but not necessarily force exact equality; if the difference is within δ, proceed with the original plan. If one arrives earlier, it may wait briefly near the landmark within a small radius until the other arrives or until the window closes. No explicit communication; coordination relies on shared landing target and tolerance-based timing.
